title: Best Budget Gaming PC (2026): 3 Picks From $600 to $1,050
description: The best budget gaming PC is the Skytech Archangel with an RTX 5060 at $850 to $1,050. Under $750, an RTX 3050 system is the floor. Picks for $500 to $800.
dek: Three budget gaming PCs, plus what $500, $600 and $800 really buy in 2026 and the cheaper routes worth knowing.
intro: A budget gaming PC in 2026 starts around $600 for a new system with a real graphics card. Below that, new prebuilts rarely include a GPU worth having, and used or refurbished systems become the better route.
These three picks cover $600 to about $1,050. The sections below explain what each budget tier buys, from $500 to $800, and how to get the most from a small budget.
quickAnswer: The best budget gaming PC is the Skytech Archangel with an RTX 5060, at about $850 to $1,050, for 1080p high settings with DLSS 4. Under $950, the iBuyPower Scale with an RTX 4060 is the value pick. Under $750, the CyberPowerPC Gamer Xtreme with an RTX 3050 is the cheapest new PC worth buying; under $600, look at used systems.

picks.label: Best Budget Gaming PC
writeup: The Archangel with an [RTX 5060](/gear/rtx-5060/) is where a budget gaming PC stops feeling like a compromise. It runs current games at 1080p high settings, supports DLSS 4 with multi frame generation, and uses standard parts that make later upgrades easy.
Check the listing for two sticks of memory and a named power supply. Its 8 GB of VRAM will need lower textures in some new games, which is the usual trade-off at this price.

picks.label: Best Under $950
picks.bestFor: 1080p gaming with a little less to spend
picks.skipIf: an RTX 5060 system costs the same
writeup: The Scale with an [RTX 4060](/gear/rtx-4060/) is a capable 1080p machine that usually costs a bit less than RTX 5060 systems. It runs most current games at 1080p high settings and draws little power, so it stays cool and quiet.
Only buy it when it is clearly cheaper than an RTX 5060 system with the same CPU, memory and storage, since the newer card is faster.

picks.label: Best Under $750
picks.skipIf: you want new AAA games at high settings
writeup: The Gamer Xtreme with an RTX 3050 is the floor for a new gaming PC worth buying. It runs Fortnite, Valorant, Counter-Strike 2, Rocket League and Minecraft well at 1080p, and its recent Core i5 is strong enough to take a much faster graphics card later.
Check whether the listing has the 6 GB or 8 GB RTX 3050; the 8 GB card is clearly faster. New AAA games need medium or low settings.
pros: Lowest price for a new PC with a GPU
cons: RTX 3050 is slow in AAA games

mentions.text: Not a budget PC, but the best next step: the Skytech Shadow with a 16 GB RTX 5060 Ti costs about $1,100 to $1,350 and lasts noticeably longer thanks to 16 GB of VRAM.
HP's Omen 16L with an RTX 5060 drops into budget territory during sales. It is compact and backed by HP support, but its HP-specific parts make upgrades harder than in the picks above.

sections.h: Can You Get a Good Gaming PC Under $500?
body: Not new, in most cases. New prebuilts under $500 usually rely on integrated graphics or a very old entry card, which handles esports at low settings but not modern games. The cheapest new systems with a real graphics card start around $600.

Under $500, the better routes are a used gaming PC with a GTX 1660, RTX 2060 or RTX 3060-class card, or a refurbished system from a major builder with a short warranty. A used PC with an RTX 3060 can outperform a new $650 RTX 3050 system. Check the GPU model, ask for a photo of the power supply label, and test it in person if you can.

If you are deciding between a $500 PC and a console, a PS5 or Xbox Series X is the stronger gaming machine at that price. Our [console GPU equivalents](/console-gpu-equivalents/) chart shows the PS5 performs roughly like an RX 6700, well above anything a new $500 PC includes.

sections.h: What Is the Best Gaming PC Under $600?
body: At $600, look for a system with an RTX 3050 8GB or similar card, a recent six-core CPU, 16 GB of memory and a 500 GB to 1 TB SSD. That is the CyberPowerPC Gamer Xtreme class, and on sale it dips toward $600.

Expect esports and older games at 1080p high, and new AAA games at low to medium settings. The value at this price is the platform: a decent CPU and case that can take a much faster graphics card later.

sections.h: What Is the Best Gaming PC Under $800?
body: Around $800, the target is an RTX 4060 system such as the iBuyPower Scale, which runs most current games at 1080p high settings. Sales sometimes bring RTX 5060 systems close to $850, and those are the better buy when the gap is small.
At this budget, check the memory layout and SSD size carefully: builders often save money with a single memory stick or a 500 GB drive, and both are worth fixing.

sections.h: Is It Cheaper to Build a Budget Gaming PC?
body: At the budget end, building saves the most when you reuse parts or buy a used graphics card. A new build with an RTX 5060, a [Ryzen 5 7600](/gear/ryzen-5-7600/), 16 GB of DDR5 and a 1 TB SSD lands close to the price of a prebuilt Archangel on sale, but with a better power supply and memory of your choice.
Memory and SSD prices have been volatile since late 2025, so compare current part prices before deciding. Our [cost guide](/how-much-does-a-gaming-pc-cost/) breaks down a typical budget build.

sections.h: Should You Buy a Used or Refurbished Budget Gaming PC?
body: Used gaming PCs are often the best value under $700, because the graphics card holds most of the value and older cards like the RTX 3060 and RX 6600 still play current games at 1080p. The risk is condition: a worn power supply or a mined-on GPU can fail early.

Refurbished systems from the original builder or a large retailer are the safer middle ground, usually with a 90-day to 1-year warranty. If you are considering paying over time instead, read our [rent-to-own guide](/rent-to-own-gaming-pc/) first: those plans usually cost far more than the PC's price.

sections.h: Which Graphics Card Matters Most in a Budget Gaming PC?
body: The graphics card decides almost everything at this price. An RTX 5060 is roughly twice as fast as an RTX 3050 in independent reviews, which is why the jump from a $650 system to a $900 one is so large. See our [budget graphics card guide](/best-budget-graphics-card/) for how the cards compare.

If you buy the cheapest system now and upgrade the card later, check the power supply first. Many budget prebuilts ship with 450 W to 550 W units, which suit an RTX 5060-class card but not much more. The [PSU calculator](/tools/psu-calculator/) shows what a planned upgrade needs.

sections.h: What Monitor Should You Pair With a Budget Gaming PC?
body: A 1080p monitor with a 144 Hz or 165 Hz refresh rate is the right match for every PC in this guide. These systems can feed high frame rates in esports at 1080p, and new AAA games run best at 1080p on these graphics cards.

A 1440p monitor is a stretch at this budget. An RTX 5060 can run lighter games at 1440p, especially with DLSS, but demanding new releases need lower settings, and the RTX 3050 and RTX 4060 are 1080p cards. Spend on the PC first and upgrade the monitor later.
If you already own a 4K TV, use it for older and lighter games at reduced resolution, or with DLSS on RTX cards, rather than expecting native 4K from a budget system.

sections.h: Where Should You Buy a Budget Gaming PC?
body: Amazon has the widest range of budget Skytech, CyberPowerPC and iBuyPower systems, while Best Buy, Walmart and Costco run regular sales on prebuilts. Costco's longer return window is valuable for a first PC, and Micro Center sells its own PowerSpec systems in its stores.

Whichever store you use, compare the specification table with the picks above rather than trusting the title, and check the return policy. Budget PCs are shipped in large boxes, and a loose graphics card or cable after delivery is common enough that a simple return process matters.

mistakes: Buying a new PC with no real graphics card
Systems sold as gaming PCs under $500 often use integrated graphics. They run esports at low settings but not modern games; a used system or a console is a better use of the money.
The 6 GB RTX 3050 is noticeably slower than the 8 GB version. Budget listings do not always make the difference obvious, so read the specification table.
Settling for a single memory stick
Budget builders often fit one 8 GB or 16 GB stick. Dual channel matters for frame rate; plan to add a matching stick if the listing has only one.
Forgetting the power supply for later upgrades
A cheap PC is a good upgrade base only if its power supply can feed a better card. Check wattage and brand before assuming you can swap the GPU later.
Budget prebuilts go on sale often. Prices that sit $100 above the usual band are common outside sale periods, so compare across stores before buying.
bottomLine: The best budget gaming PC is the Skytech Archangel with an RTX 5060 at about $850 to $1,050, which handles current games at 1080p high settings. The iBuyPower Scale with an RTX 4060 is the pick under $950, and the CyberPowerPC Gamer Xtreme with an RTX 3050 is the cheapest new gaming PC worth buying, under $750. Below $600, a used or refurbished system, or a console, gives better gaming performance for the money.

faqs.q: What is the best budget gaming PC?
faqs.a: The Skytech Archangel with an RTX 5060, at about $850 to $1,050. It runs current games at 1080p high settings with DLSS 4 and is easy to upgrade later.

faqs.q: Can you get a gaming PC for $500?
faqs.a: Not a good new one in most cases. New systems at $500 usually lack a real graphics card. A used PC with an RTX 3060-class card, or a console, is better value at that price.

faqs.q: What is the best gaming PC under $600?
faqs.a: A system with an RTX 3050 8GB and a recent six-core CPU, such as the CyberPowerPC Gamer Xtreme on sale. It handles esports at 1080p and is a good base for a later GPU upgrade.

faqs.q: What can a budget gaming PC run?
faqs.a: An RTX 5060 system runs current games at 1080p high settings. An RTX 3050 system runs esports well but needs low to medium settings in new AAA games.

faqs.q: Is a budget gaming PC better than a console?
faqs.a: Under about $800, a PS5 is usually the stronger gaming machine. From the RTX 5060 tier up, a PC matches or beats a PS5 and adds cheaper games, mods and upgrades.

faqs.q: Is a cheap gaming PC worth it?
faqs.a: Yes, if it has a real graphics card, two sticks of memory and a decent power supply. A cheap PC with integrated graphics is not worth it for gaming.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to get a gaming PC?
faqs.a: A used system with an RTX 30-series or RX 6000-series card, bought locally and tested in person. Refurbished systems with a short warranty are the safer alternative.

faqs.q: Can I upgrade a budget gaming PC later?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Memory and storage are easy to add. A graphics card upgrade depends on the power supply's wattage and connectors, so check those first.

ranking.intro: These picks are built from manufacturer and retailer specifications, published independent reviews of the graphics cards and CPUs inside, and owner reports on retailer sites and forums. Nothing here was bench-tested by Enthusiast Review. Prebuilt configurations change often, sometimes under the same product name, so every pick names the GPU tier it was judged at and lists what to confirm in the listing.
criteria: The GPU decides gaming performance, so systems were judged first on which card they carry and how its street price compares with the whole PC's price.
8 GB cards already need lower texture settings in some new games. Systems with 12 GB and 16 GB cards scored higher at each tier.
A named power supply with headroom, two sticks of memory and a standard motherboard make a prebuilt last longer and easier to upgrade.
The processor should be strong enough that it does not hold the graphics card back in common games.
Warranty terms, retail availability and owner reports on shipping damage and support were weighed where systems were otherwise close.
